children: US stock futures fell more than 1.5 per cent on Monday afternoon, pointing to a weak start for equities, as oil prices surged on supply concerns in West Asia and investors braced for possible interest rate hikes in the United States and Japan this week.
AI-linked shares came under additional pressure after the leaders of OpenAI and Anthropic called for a slowdown in AI development to manage risks and protect humanity.
At 1:30 pm IST, S&P 500 futures were down 0.67 per cent, while Nasdaq futures fell 1.52 per cent. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures declined 0.22 per cent.

On the oil front, Brent crude climbed nearly 3 per cent after fresh strikes on Saudi Arabia and ships in the Gulf. An attack on a Saudi oil pipeline and an advance by Yemen's Houthis raised concerns over further disruption to global energy supplies.
Brent futures were last up 2.5 per cent at USD 107.18 a barrel, after gaining nearly 9 per cent last week. US crude rose 2.6 per cent to USD 102.62 a barrel.
A meeting in Oman between Iran and Gulf Arab states, scheduled for Monday to discuss a deal on opening the Strait of Hormuz, was postponed.

An uncomfortably hot US consumer price report on Friday led markets to price in an 86 per cent chance that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates by 25 basis points on Wednesday and move again by December. It would be the first hike since mid-2023.
Japan's Nikkei fell 1 per cent, while South Korea's benchmark dropped 3.2 per cent amid concerns over a slowdown in AI development.
Indian markets remained closed on Monday on the occasion of Ganesh Chaturthi.

title: Nasdaq futures fall over 1.5% as oil climbs; AI stocks decline amid safety debate
